subject: Materials Science
title: Brinell Hardness: The Ball Test
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Brinell Hardness: The Ball Test.

hook.text: Press a hard steel ball into a metal surface, measure the dent — that's the Brinell hardness test.

buildup.text: A 10mm ball is pressed in with a known force (typically 3,000 kg) and the indentation diameter is measured.

discovery.text: BHN = force ÷ indentation surface area — bigger dent means softer material.

twist.text: Brinell averages over a large area — great for cast iron with graphite flakes that would fool smaller tests.

climax.text: Johan Brinell invented it in 1900 for Swedish steelworks — it's still used worldwide over a century later.

punchline.text: Push a ball, measure the dent — hardness in a single number.

quiz.question: What does the Brinell test measure?
options: How far a material stretches before breaking
Resistance to indentation by a hard ball under known force
The elastic modulus of the material
